newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Two Red Cross hostages released in Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: Two Red Cross hostages released in Tajikistan.

text.p: Two Red Cross employees, kidnapped by rebels in the former Soviet republic of Tajikistan, were released on Friday while the government said it expected remaining hostages to be freed later in the day.
A U.N. spokesman in Tajikistan told Reuters that the two, British national Elizabeth Trinch and her Tajik translator, had already returned to Dushanbe.
"They are being released without preconditions," Thomas Merkelbach, head of the ICRC (International Committee of the Red Cross) mission in the war-ravaged country, told a news conference in Dushanbe.
The Red Cross suspended operations after four employees with the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR), including a Nigerian national, were kidnapped in the capital Dushanbe on Thursday.
The spokesman said the UNHCR workers, four U.N. military observers -- from Austria, Switzerland and Ukraine -- and four Russian journalists were still being held by the group.
The hostage-takers are part of a group commanded by Rizvon Sadirov, who used to fight for the Islamic opposition but whose loyalties are now unclear.
The kidnappings were carried out by Rizvon's brother Bakhrom Sadirov, who is demanding free passage for other members based in neighbouring Afghanistan to return to Tajikistan.
Earlier on Friday, the Tajik government said other hostages may also be released.
"The negotiations are hopeful," Zafar Saidov, spokesman for Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov, said. "The others are expected to be released tonight," he said.
Saidov said the head of the presidential guard, Gafar Mirzoyev, was on his way to negotiate with the rebels.
On Thursday, Russian officials threatened to use force to free the hostages.
However, Saidov said force was not being considered. "By no means will military force be used," he said.

Tajikistan, a mountainous country bordering China, has been racked by a bitter four-year civil war but a ceasefire agreed between the government and the armed Islamic opposition last December appears to be holding.
